newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian industrialists see slow growth, CPI higher.
newsitem.headline: Italian industrialists see slow growth, CPI higher.

text.p: The Italian economy is set to grow more slowly than previously expected, while inflation will climb back above three percent next year, industrialists' group Confindustria said in a report on Wednesday.

The survey forecasts gross domestic product (GDP) will rise just 0.7 percent this year, 1.2 percent in 1997 and 2.3 percent in 1998, against government forecasts of 0.8 percent, two percent and 2.8 percent, respectively.
Confindustria also said inflation would increase an average 3.8 percent this year, dipping to 2.8 percent in 1997 and to 2.6 percent in 1998.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government has predicted inflation at 3.9 percent this year, 2.5 percent next year and two percent the year after.

The employers' organisation, which openly disagreed with the Prodi administration on a number of issues, said the process of dis-inflation, which started in 1995, should end during the course of next year.
It said prices would continue to fall in the first months of 1997, with the exception of January, when an increase was expected due to statistical reasons.
"Then, there will be another climb above three percent in the middle months of the year," it predicted.
Year-on-year inflation was 2.6 percent in November.
Confindustria said that in the last part of this year the recent fall in economic activity had been halted, but warned that it was too soon to talk about a recovery.
Confindustria chief economist Giampaolo Galli said the economic pick-up in the rest of Europe would boost exports which would in turn help the entire Italian economy.

Further help for Italian companies would come from a further cut in official rates before the end of the year, Confindustria said. However it warned that money market rates might rise again next year. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
